**Security: pass-with-notes**, final round at `7da7b5320602a686d4021d4661aca861d76c4c1b`, against `49c151a5d3bcb1e6725e61a257cf0895b9752c58`, under C33/C34.

Cheap revive now requires a known cold cache and refuses missing facts before lifecycle writes. The shared helper preserves ordinary warmth detection. No scoped security vulnerability or remaining normal-use blocking bug was established.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No scoped vulnerabilities found | - |

## Delta verified

`cache_known` distinguishes known warm/cold from unknown, returning only static reason strings for unbound, unsupported, absent/failed session facts, missing last call and missing TTL. The daemon adds the existing three-second status bound; timeout likewise returns fixed text, not a transcript or adapter diagnostic.

`is_warm` is now `cache_known(...) == Ok(true)`. For known facts it uses exactly the previous expression: `now < last_call.saturating_add(min(ttl, COLD_IDLE_MS))`. Unknown remains not-warm for ordinary guard behavior; exact expiry, future calls and saturating arithmetic therefore retain their prior semantics.

Only `Ok(false)` permits cheap revive. Warm or unknown status refuses `E-RS-REVIVE-CHEAP` before any tombstone, relaunch or compact write. Fixed Sonnet selection, explicit-only invocation and ordinary compact/authority paths remain as previously reviewed.

The disclosed compact-half failure still leaves the successful Sonnet revive running and uncompacted. This is not a live model/billing or deployment proof. No new C34 hardening gate was added.

## Evidence

The helper assessment supplied no supporting detail; the complete own repair `87bb2dbfbf1ebdb8abbc5a58f9dc6db3cbb133c8` was directly inspected. Main merges were not treated as new F154 changes. Local/remote/GitHub heads agree; detached shared worktree clean.

CI [42576508720](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42576508720) succeeded on retry, checking merge `9598f928c2baddd4ad6971520f4b3df47fe118d3`, with this head and main `f7744c5c3f677732af8b3c0a4dad657544811ce0` as parents; tree `d25db733f287427abafc8a9fbaf18ccb54135a11`.

The successful job's upload log names JUnit artifact **13654869689**, not the numerically larger artifact from the earlier failed attempt. That exact artifact confirms 2,342 passing cases, no failures; six separately skipped. Extended cheap-refusal cases and core warmth/boundary cases executed successfully. Current code checks succeed; an earlier Delivers run was cancelled.

The unrelated teardown flake is not a new security finding. No local builds/tests, mutants, credential reads or live-system probes were performed.
